title: AMD–Chinese joint venture
wikitext:
{{Short description|none}}
The '''AMD–Chinese joint venture''' is the [[joint venture|agreement]] between the American semiconductor company [[Advanced Micro Devices]] (AMD) and China-based partners to license and build [[x86]]-compatible [[CPU]]s for the Chinese-based market.<ref name="Alcorn 2018">{{cite news |last1=Alcorn |first1=Paul |date=July 6, 2018 |title=China Finds Zen: Begins Production Of x86 Processors Based On AMD's IP |url=https://www.tomshardware.com/news/china-zen-x86-processor-dryhana,37417.html |website=Tom's Hardware |language=en-US |access-date=July 9, 2018}}</ref><ref name="Larabel 2018">{{cite news |last1=Larabel |first1=Michael |date=June 9, 2018 |title=Hygon Dhyana: Chinese x86 Server CPUs Based On AMD Zen |url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=Hygon-Dhyana-AMD-China-CPUs |website=Phoronix |language=en-US |access-date=July 9, 2018}}</ref> China has been unable to produce a CPU based on its own  technology;<ref>{{cite news |last=Clark |first=Don |date=April 21, 2016 |title=AMD to License Chip Technology to China Chip Venture|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/amd-to-license-chip-technology-to-china-chip-venture-1461269701 |website=The Wall Street Journal |access-date=April 24, 2018 |quote="The VIA/Shanghai Zhaoxin KX-5000 series of x86-compatible CPUs will never be sold outside of China to avoid an Intel lawsuit.","...will use the technology to develop chips for server systems to be sold only in China"}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Wu |first1=Yimian |date=May 23, 2018 |title=China Supports Local Semiconductor Firms By Adding Them To Government Procurement List |url=https://www.chinamoneynetwork.com/2018/05/23/china-supports-local-semiconductor-firms-by-adding-them-to-government-procurement-list |website=China Money Network |access-date=May 31, 2018}}</ref> This is significant because the joint venture was negotiated and agreed to well before the 2018 [[China–United States trade war|trade war between the US and China]]<ref name="Alcorn 2018" /> and the international chip shortage of the early 2020s. Unlike Taiwan, China does not have an established or lucrative microchip industry or even capabilities for that matter. It is similar to the [[Zhaoxin]] joint venture supported by [[VIA Technologies]].<ref name="2018-ars-technica">{{cite news |last1=Gallagher |first1=Sean |date=July 9, 2018 |title=China producing x86 chips nearly identical to AMD server processors |url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2018/07/china-producing-x86-chips-nearly-identical-to-amd-server-processors/ |website=Ars Technica |language=en-US |access-date=July 11, 2018}}</ref> Unlike other industries in which China naturally excels, the microchip industry requires significant research and development.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ravi |first=Sarah |date=2022-09-16 |title=American Semiconductor Research: Leadership Through Innovation |url=https://www.semiconductors.org/american-semiconductor-research-leadership-through-innovation/ |access-date=2023-01-13 |website=Semiconductor Industry Association |language=en-US}}</ref> 

== Structure ==
{{Main|Hygon Information Technology}}
AMD has received permission from the US Department of Defense and Department of Commerce to export the [[Zen (microarchitecture)|Zen 1 core design]] to China.<ref name="CutressWilson">{{Cite web |last1=Cutress |first1=Ian |last2=Wilson |first2=Wendell |date=February 27, 2020 |title=Testing a Chinese x86 CPU: A Deep Dive into Zen-based Hygon Dhyana Processors |url=https://www.anandtech.com/show/15493/hygon-dhyana-reviewed-chinese-x86-cpus-amd |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227142243/https://www.anandtech.com/show/15493/hygon-dhyana-reviewed-chinese-x86-cpus-amd |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 27, 2020 |website=AnandTech |language=en-US |access-date=September 29, 2020}}</ref> Due to legal restrictions AMD has set up multiple companies to allow licensing of [[x86]] technology to China. The overarching joint venture is the [[Tianjin Haiguang Advanced Technology Investment Co. Ltd.]] (THATIC).<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/> THATIC is owned by "AMD and both public and private Chinese companies, including the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]":<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/> however its major share is reportedly owned by AMD itself.<ref name="CutressWilson" />

The joint-venture set up Haiguang Microelectronics Co. Ltd. (HMC) and Chengdu Haiguang Integrated Circuit Design Co. Ltd. (Hygon), with controlling stakes being held by AMD and THATIC respectively.<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/><ref name="CutressWilson"/> HMC owns the local intellectual property and subcontracts manufacturing for the chip, while Hygon designs the chip and markets and sells the processors.<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/>

== History ==
The joint venture was announced by AMD in 2016.<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/> The first processor was released in 2018.<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/> At the [[Computex]] 2019 trade show, AMD CEO [[Lisa Su]] confirmed that the licence will be limited to the original Zen architecture, and would not be extended to Zen 2.<ref name="Alcorn 2019">{{cite news |last=Alcorn |first=Paul |date=June 4, 2019 |title=AMD Not Conducting Further Technology Transfers of x86 IP to China JV |url=https://www.tomshardware.com/news/amd-zen-china-x86-ip-license,39573.html |website=Tom's Hardware |language=en-US |access-date=4 June 2019}}</ref>

On June 24, 2019, the U.S. government placed one of the parent companies, and thus the joint venture, on its export control [[Entity List]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Alcorn |first=Paul |date=June 21, 2019 |title=U.S. Will Add AMD's China Joint Venture to Entity List, Cut Access to U.S. Technology (Updated) |url=https://www.tomshardware.com/news/amd-joint-venture-partner-banned-us-trade-war,39703.html |website=Tom's Hardware |language=en-US |access-date=October 20, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{USFR|84|29371}}</ref> which bans further technology transfers from AMD and possibly{{CN|date=October 2019}} hampers its existing operations. The opinion of Anandtech is that further AMD involvement in the joint venture will be minimal due to the ban.<ref name="CutressWilson"/>

== Microprocessors ==
=== Hygon SOC ===
The initial microprocessor created in 2018 is the [[AMD Epyc#Chinese_variants|Hygon Dhyana]] [[system on a chip]].<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/><ref name="Larabel 2018"/> It is noted to be a variant of the AMD [[Epyc]] and is so similar that "there is little to no differentiation between the chips."<ref name="Alcorn 2018"/> It has been noted that there is "less than 200 lines of new kernel code" for [[Linux]] kernel support, and that the Dhyana is "mostly a re-branded Zen CPU for the Chinese server market."<ref name="Larabel 2018"/>

Testing in 2020 suggested that "integer performance is essentially identical, however the floating point and [[RDRAND]] and [[RDRAND|RDSEED]] instructions' performance has been reduced" from the equivalent Zen 1 processor.<ref name="CutressWilson"/> The cryptography extensions like [[AES instruction set|AES]] have been replaced by Chinese versions called SM2, [[SM3 (hash function)|SM3]] and [[SM4 (cipher)|SM4]] which are according to Anandtech are very similar to [[Elliptic-curve cryptography|ECC]](-based), [[SHA-2|SHA-256]] and [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES-128]] algorithms respectively.<ref name="CutressWilson"/> [[Advanced Vector Extensions|AVX/AVX2]] was also disabled, but the research has suspected that it happened due to a bug rather than was done intentionally.<ref name="CutressWilson"/>
